title: The password checker that fails closed
prompt:
Implement `check_password(pw)` returning `(ok, problems)` — `ok` True iff ALL rules pass, `problems` a list of human-readable violation strings in this fixed order:

1. `'must be at least 12 characters'` when `len(pw) < 12`
2. `'must contain an uppercase letter'` when no `A-Z`
3. `'must contain a lowercase letter'` when no `a-z`
4. `'must contain a digit'` when no digit
5. `'must not contain whitespace'` when any whitespace
6. `'must not be a known breached password'` when lowercased in the fixed set `{"password123456", "correcthorsebattery", "letmein123456"}`

An empty password fails rules 1-4 (and rule 5 not, rule 6 not). Non-string input → `('must be a string',)`-style handling: return `(False, ['must be a string'])`.

tests.name: strong passes, weak fails with the full list
tests.code:
ok, problems = check_password('Str0ng-Passphrase!')
assert ok is True and problems == []
ok, problems = check_password('short')
assert ok is False
assert problems == ['must be at least 12 characters', 'must contain an uppercase letter', 'must contain a digit']
print('ok')
tests.hint: 'short' is too small, lacks uppercase and a digit — reported in order.

tests.name: breach list and whitespace, fail closed
tests.code:
ok, problems = check_password('correcthorsebattery')
assert ok is False and problems == ['must contain an uppercase letter', 'must contain a digit', 'must not be a known breached password']
ok, problems = check_password('has space inside 12')
assert ok is False and 'must not contain whitespace' in problems
ok, problems = check_password(None)
assert ok is False and problems == ['must be a string']
print('ok')
tests.hint: Breached + missing classes all reported; wrong type fails closed.
